title: Salsa Verde
subtitle: tangy green tomatillo sauce
excerpt: A sharp, lightly cooked green sauce made from tomatillos, chilli, garlic, and coriander. It takes 20 minutes and goes with almost everything -- tacos, grilled meat, eggs, or as a dipping sauce.
sourceNotes: Salsa verde is one of Mexico's most ancient condiments. The tomatillo, a small green fruit encased in a papery husk, has been cultivated in Mexico since pre-Columbian times.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead and store in the fridge in a sealed jar.

content.text: Simmering the tomatillos briefly mellows their sharp raw flavour. Do not overcook them -- they should keep a little brightness. Blend the sauce while hot for a smoother result.

items.prepNote: use 400g tomatillos (tinned) or unripe green tomatoes
use a handful of fresh coriander leaves

content.text: Put the tomatillos, onion, garlic, and chilli in a saucepan. Cover with cold water.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes until the tomatillos are soft.
Drain, reserving a little of the cooking liquid. Transfer to a blender.
Add the fresh coriander, lime juice, and salt. Blend until smooth. Add a splash of cooking liquid to loosen if needed.
Taste and adjust the salt and lime. Serve at room temperature or chilled.

items.cause: Tomatillos undercooked or too little salt
items.fix: Simmer for a few more minutes to soften the acidity. A pinch of sugar also helps balance sharpness.

items.symptom: Salsa is dull and lacks brightness
items.cause: Overcooked or too much cooking liquid retained
items.fix: Add a squeeze of fresh lime juice after blending. Fresh coriander added after blending also lifts the colour.
Blend in a little extra cooking water until it reaches a pourable consistency.

content.text: Salsa verde is one of Mexico's oldest condiments. The tomatillo has been cultivated in Mexico since long before European contact. Green salsas appear across all regions of the country in different forms. This version -- simmered then blended -- is common in central Mexico and pairs well with pork, chicken, and eggs.
